description: REGIME MAP, decode arm. output_len=64 so decode dominates; decode_ms/64 is the per-decode-step cost, measured against n. Every cost number in this project comes from prefill-dominated work, and decode is where production serving spends its time.
note_gap: n=11..14 were never measured. At prompt_len 512 the sparse sweep jumped from 5120 tokens (n=10, ~89 ms) to 7680 (n=15, ~158 ms), so the SHAPE of the cost curve across that range is unknown -- and it is exactly the range where request padding (all of 9..16 pad to 16) and token padding (4608..8192 all pad to 8192) predict a flat cost while the measurements do not. Filling it is what makes a refit possible rather than a guess.
note_budget: n=16 x 512 = 8192 tokens is exactly max_num_batched_tokens, so n<=16 is one scheduler step and n=18 must split into two. The split cell is kept deliberately: it is the only direct evidence of what a two-step dispatch costs.
note_verification: The flag is not in vLLM's engine-config line, so the audit cannot see it. It IS verifiable from the warmup log: with the flag on, 'Prepared attn request paddings' prints the full ladder instead of [256]. Check that before trusting this run.
note_expectation: RPA is a ragged kernel, so a padded request dimension should cost little even at 256 -- the padded slots hold no KV blocks. The likely finding is a large compile-time increase for little or no runtime change, which would explain why the default is off. A runtime WIN would be the more actionable result: the default leaves performance on the table.
